correctness.rationale: The endpoint-alphabet argument bounds the singleton case by nine. The two-endpoint case is exhaustively represented by twenty reverse-complement orbits; six isolated orbit vertices contribute eight, four weight-two triangles and a weight-one pair bound the remaining contribution by nine. A 17-word witness attains the bound. Enumerating only 162 clique-equality combinations gives eight fixed-endpoint maximum designs; complement-preserving relabeling yields 32 labeled maxima in four orbits of size eight. Source code and an independent full 2^20 subset census check all critical finite steps.

originality.rationale: The exact object is not the ordinary q=4,n=4 non-overlapping code problem: it adds closure under Watson--Crick reverse complement, changes the maximum from the published unrestricted 27 to 17, and determines 32 symmetry-classified equality codes. Blackburn gives the non-overlap framework, while Stanovnik--Moškon--Mraz Theorems 19--20 give only the unrestricted maximum and its unrestricted maxima. Multiple alias/parameter checks did not identify an implication or exact table. An unindexed earlier result remains a qualified priority risk.
residual_risks: A specialized strand-invariant cross-bifix-free maximum could occur in unindexed DNA-code literature under other terminology.

value.rationale: Full frame synchronization together with obligatory inclusion of both Watson--Crick strand orientations is a natural two-strand codebook design requirement; four-mers are the shortest small DNA case with nontrivial length-two and length-three prefix/suffix interactions. The constrained maximum 17 versus ordinary 27 and four structurally distinct equality designs give an exact capacity and complete design-space classification, not an arbitrary parameter table. These are mathematical, not physical, claims.
